dependency_coverage.name: Bool.true

dependency_coverage.name: Eq

dependency_coverage.name: Exists

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace

dependency_coverage.name: ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid

binders: There exists a real constant c.
ι is an arbitrary finite type of indices.
Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is an arbitrary probability measure on Ω.
B is an arbitrary indexed family of Boolean-valued functions B_i : Ω -> Bool.
p is an arbitrary indexed family of nonnegative real parameters p_i.
δ is an arbitrary real number introduced after the independence, law, and measurability assumptions.
hypotheses: The existential constant is strictly positive: c > 0.
For every index i, p_i <= 1; since p_i is a nonnegative real by type, 0 <= p_i <= 1.
The entire indexed family (B_i) is mutually independent under μ.
For every i, B_i has under μ the Boolean Bernoulli law assigning probability p_i to true and 1 - p_i to false.
For every i, B_i is measurable into the discrete measurable space on Bool.
conclusions: The real probability of the event {omega | δ * sum_i p_i <= |sum_i 1_{B_i(omega)=true} - sum_i p_i|} is at most 2 * exp(-c * (sum_i p_i) * δ^2).
The same one positive constant c works uniformly for every choice of finite index type, probability space, independent Bernoulli family, admissible success parameters, and δ in (0, 1].
mathematical_definitions: For each sample point omega, X(omega) = sum_i 1_{B_i(omega)=true} is the real-valued count of true outcomes.
S = sum_i p_i is the sum of the Bernoulli success parameters and hence the center used in the stated deviation event.
The deviation event is {|X - S| >= δ S}; its boundary is included.
The Bernoulli law on Bool puts mass p_i at true and mass 1 - p_i at false.
μ.real converts the finite extended-nonnegative measure of the event to its ordinary real probability.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every finite family of mutually independent measurable Bernoulli Boolean random variables with possibly different success probabilities p_i, and every real relative-deviation parameter 0 < δ <= 1, the probability that the number of successes differs from the total success parameter sum by at least δ times that sum is at most 2 exp(-c δ^2 sum_i p_i).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The family must be finite, but its finite index type is otherwise arbitrary and may be empty.
Each p_i may equal 0 or 1; only 0 <= p_i <= 1 is required, and the nonnegativity comes from the NNReal type.
The bound covers only relative-deviation parameters 0 < δ <= 1 and does not state the same formula for δ > 1 or δ = 0.
The event uses an inclusive threshold, |X - S| >= δ S, and is two-sided because of the absolute value.
The center and scale are S = sum_i p_i; no separate variance term or identical-distribution assumption is encoded.

If S = 0, then the threshold is zero and the event is the whole sample space because |X - S| >= 0; the asserted inequality becomes 1 <= 2, so this degenerate case is valid but uninformative rather than vacuous.
The constant c is existentially quantified before all other data, so it cannot depend on the family, probability space, parameters, or δ; its numerical value is not specified.
The conclusion is only an upper tail bound on the absolute deviation probability; it provides no matching lower bound or claim of optimal constants.
